conclusion_qualitative: This skill (no name given; the file is named by its hash) is a fix-and-guard workflow: it records a bug as a tracked item, has a subagent fix it, and adds or repairs a regression test so the bug cannot return unnoticed. The agent fixes bugs on its own without asking permission, but must use a separate worktree instead of `main` unless the fix is a production hotfix. It runs the regression test and confirms it passes before committing. It never tells the agent to ask the user for information, wait for approval, or what to do when something fails.

When the agent notices a bug mid-session it must not ask permission or ask "should I fix this?"; it starts the fix right away. It must not fix on `main` when working in a worktree (a separate working copy) would be safe, unless it is a real production hotfix, and must not clutter the team's external tracker with one-line fixes.

statements.quote: You (the orchestrator) notice a problem mid-session — **don't ask permission, fire `/fix`** and route the work
Don't gate behind "should I fix this?" — if it's a bug, fix it.
For routine fixes (typos, small logic bugs caught in review), the bead itself is the record — don't clutter the external tracker with one-line fixes.
**Fix on main when worktree isolation would have been safe** — unless it's a true production hotfix, use the worktree.
